items.en: Board of Peace warns Gaza ceasefire faces imminent collapse without action
items.zh: 和平委員會警告：加薩停火瀕臨崩潰
items.summary: The US-led Board of Peace has warned that the Gaza ceasefire agreed in 2025 is close to collapse unless the parties act quickly. In its statement the board decried continued fighting inside Gaza and criticised repeated delays in implementing the terms of the deal, including the opening of crossings and the handover of security responsibilities. Members said the truce has been eroded by near-daily strikes and by disputes over who governs the territory. The warning follows the board's first formal meeting, which produced broad pledges but few binding commitments, leaving aid agencies uncertain about whether access to the enclave will improve.

items.en: What is Trump hoping to achieve at APEC meeting in China?
items.zh: 川普赴中出席 APEC，將與習、普三方會談
items.summary: US President Donald Trump has arrived in China for the APEC summit, where he is expected to meet Chinese leader Xi Jinping for the third time this year and to hold a trilateral meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin. Analysts say Washington wants movement on tariffs, rare earth supplies and advanced chip exports, while Beijing is using the venue to present itself as the defender of open trade. The trilateral format is unusual and has unsettled European capitals, which fear bargaining over Ukraine. Trump has also raised new global tariffs to fifteen percent as legal fights over refunds continue.

items.en: Mary Peltola flips Alaska Senate seat in another Democratic win
items.zh: 佩爾托拉翻轉阿拉斯加參議席，民主黨再勝
items.summary: Democrat Mary Peltola has won Alaska's US Senate seat, the last race to be called in this year's midterm elections, flipping a seat long held by Republicans. The contest was decided by a narrow margin after ranked-choice tabulation and is likely to face legal challenges over ballot handling and counting procedures. Peltola, a former congresswoman, campaigned on fisheries, energy permitting and the cost of living in rural communities. Her victory narrows the Republican margin in the chamber and gives Democrats more leverage over nominations and spending bills heading into the new session.

items.en: Australia issues sanctions targeting Israeli settlers
items.zh: 澳洲制裁以色列定居者及相關組織
items.summary: Australia has imposed targeted sanctions on three Israeli individuals and four organisations that Canberra says are driving illegal settlement expansion in the occupied West Bank. The measures include travel bans and asset freezes, and follow similar steps by several European governments over the past two years. Australian officials said settlement growth and settler violence undermine prospects for a two-state outcome and breach international law. Israel's government rejected the decision as unjustified interference. Rights groups welcomed the move but urged Australia to go further by restricting trade with settlement-based businesses and reviewing defence cooperation agreements.

items.en: Rafael Grossi wants to be UN chief. Will Trump's support nuke his chances?
items.zh: 葛羅西競逐聯合國秘書長，川普支持反成變數
items.summary: Rafael Grossi, head of the International Atomic Energy Agency, is campaigning to become the next United Nations secretary-general. Diplomats describe him as technically competent and a skilled negotiator after years of handling Iran's nuclear file, but say questions remain about his vision for reforming a cash-strapped organisation. His candidacy has been complicated by visible backing from the Trump administration, which some member states see as disqualifying rather than helpful. Several governments in the Global South argue the next secretary-general should come from Latin America, while others are pressing for the first woman to hold the post.

items.en: Waymo suspends driverless freeway rides across US after California ban
items.zh: 加州禁令後，Waymo 全美暫停高速公路無人駕駛
items.summary: Waymo has suspended driverless rides on freeways across the United States after California regulators declared self-driving cars an imminent hazard to public safety and barred the company from highway operations in the state. The order followed a series of traffic incidents, including collisions and vehicles stopping in live lanes. Waymo said it would pause freeway service nationwide while it reviews data and works with regulators, keeping surface-street operations running. The decision is a setback for the industry's push into higher-speed driving, and rival operators now face pressure to show that their highway systems can handle unexpected road conditions.

items.en: Rubio rules out cyberattacks or links between tech outages
items.zh: 魯比歐否認科技斷線與網路攻擊有關
items.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said there is no evidence that the recent wave of technology outages was caused by cyberattacks or that the incidents are connected to one another. The disruptions have hit airline systems, federal aviation tools and widely used cloud services, grounding flights and interrupting payments in several states. Rubio said investigators are treating each case separately and have so far found configuration errors and failed software updates rather than hostile intrusion. Lawmakers remain unconvinced and have demanded briefings, warning that the concentration of critical services in a few providers is itself the risk.

items.en: Markwayne Mullin faces scrutiny as administration grapples with unsettling tech outages
items.zh: 馬爾文受質詢，政府應對連串科技斷線
items.summary: Markwayne Mullin is facing sharp questioning over the administration's handling of a string of technology failures that disrupted air traffic systems and other federal services. Lawmakers from both parties pressed for a clear account of what broke, how long recovery took and whether staffing cuts and deferred maintenance at key agencies made the outages worse. Officials have described the failures as separate software and configuration problems rather than a coordinated attack, but have struggled to explain why backups did not take over. Congress is now weighing new reporting requirements and resilience standards for critical federal technology contracts.

items.en: FIFA election: Who are Infantino's challengers, and will he be re-elected?
items.zh: FIFA 主席選舉：因凡蒂諾的挑戰者是誰
items.summary: FIFA has opened nominations for its presidential election, with Gianni Infantino seeking a fourth term at the head of world football's governing body. Three challengers have emerged, including candidates backed by African and Asian federations, and each must gather declarations of support from member associations before the ballot. Infantino remains the heavy favourite given his control of the expanded World Cup calendar and FIFA's revenue growth, but critics point to governance concerns and his closeness to political leaders. The vote will set the direction for club competition reform, prize money distribution and the future shape of the international match calendar.

items.en: Photos: India defeat Pakistan to win SAFF Championship in Bangladesh
items.zh: 印度擊敗巴基斯坦，奪下 SAFF 錦標賽冠軍
items.summary: India beat Pakistan in the final of the South Asian Football Federation Championship in Bangladesh, adding another regional title to their record in the competition. The match drew a large crowd in Dhaka and heavy security, given the political tension between the two countries, and was decided by a tight scoreline after a cautious opening half. Indian players celebrated with fans on the pitch, while Pakistan's squad took encouragement from reaching their first final in years after a long period of suspension and rebuilding. The result strengthens India's position as the dominant side in South Asian football.

items.en: Hungary on the hunt for a football hero
items.zh: 北愛爾蘭 1-1 逼和匈牙利，拿下升級資格
items.summary: Northern Ireland secured promotion in the UEFA Nations League after drawing one-all with Hungary, a result that leaves the Hungarian side still searching for a player to carry the team through tight qualifying nights. Hungary took the lead but conceded late and have now dropped points in successive home fixtures, prompting renewed debate about squad depth beyond their established stars. Northern Ireland's coach praised his players' discipline and said the promotion rewards a long rebuilding effort. The draw reshapes the group standings and gives Northern Ireland a better seeding for the next qualification cycle.

items.en: At the origin of France's education protests, students refuse to give up
items.zh: 法國教育抗爭源頭：學生拒絕放棄
items.summary: Students at the heart of France's education protests say they will keep demonstrating despite police pressure and the start of exam season. The movement began over cuts to teaching posts and changes to admissions rules, and has since widened into complaints about overcrowded classrooms, mental health support and the cost of student housing. Pupils describe blockades and sit-ins organised through group chats, while teachers' unions have joined some of the walkouts. The government says the reforms are needed to control spending and improve results, but has signalled it may delay parts of the package to calm campuses.

items.en: Protests as Jason Arday's accuser speaks at Oxford University
items.zh: 牛津演講引抗議，學術抄襲爭議升溫
items.summary: Hundreds of people protested outside an Oxford University venue as Nathan Cofnas, who has accused the sociologist Jason Arday of plagiarism, spoke at an event on campus. Demonstrators argued the invitation lent a platform to views they consider racist, while organisers defended it on academic freedom grounds. The dispute has become a flashpoint in a wider British debate about how universities handle misconduct allegations, who adjudicates them and how quickly findings are published. Staff groups say unclear procedures leave both accusers and the accused in limbo for months, damaging trust in institutional investigations.

items.en: Why SNL's 'Sister' sketch hit a nerve about the reality of caregiving
items.zh: SNL 短劇戳中照顧者的真實心理壓力
items.summary: A Saturday Night Live sketch about two sisters dividing care for an ageing parent has resonated widely because it names the resentment, guilt and exhaustion that family caregivers rarely discuss openly. Psychologists quoted in the piece say caregiving burden often falls unevenly on one sibling, usually a daughter, and that the imbalance breeds long-lasting family conflict. They recommend explicit agreements about tasks and money, scheduled respite, and naming the emotional load rather than treating it as a personal failing. Comedy, they argue, gives people permission to admit feelings they judge themselves for having.

items.en: Nvidia shoots down calls for Jensen Huang's return amid strong earnings
items.zh: 輝達財報強勁，董事會排除黃仁勳回任
items.summary: Nvidia's board chair said the company does not intend to reinstate Jensen Huang, rejecting investor calls for his return even as the chipmaker reported strong results and guided to about one hundred and thirty billion dollars of revenue in the fourth quarter. Management credited demand for data-centre accelerators and said supply of advanced packaging is improving. Despite the beat, the shares fell for a fifth straight session as investors questioned AI valuations and the sustainability of customer capital spending. The guidance matters for Taiwan's supply chain, where foundry, CoWoS packaging, board and cooling suppliers track Nvidia's order outlook closely.

items.en: Bessent vs Lutnick: Who is winning the China chip debate?
items.zh: 貝森特對盧特尼克：對中晶片政策誰占上風
items.summary: Two senior figures in the Trump administration are pulling US chip policy in opposite directions. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent favours using export approvals as leverage in trade talks with Beijing, while Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick pushes tighter controls on advanced accelerators and the tools to make them. The outcome determines whether Nvidia and its peers can ship high-end parts such as the H200 to Chinese buyers, and how far restrictions reach Chinese firms operating outside China. Companies complain the shifting line makes planning impossible, and allied governments say they are being asked to match rules that keep changing.

items.en: Mrs. GREEN APPLE's Ringo Jam Tour 'SHADOWS' plays Nagano Big Hat on November 18 and 19
items.zh: Mrs. GREEN APPLE 巡演長野 Big Hat 連兩場
items.summary: Mrs. GREEN APPLE are midway through the Ringo Jam Tour 'SHADOWS', their first arena tour in about three years, which supports the sixth original album released at the end of September. The run covers twenty-eight dates in Japan and reaches Nagano's Wakasato Big Hat arena on November 18 and 19, before Chiba, Hyogo, Fukuoka, Miyagi, Kanagawa and a year-end finale at Aichi Sky Expo on December 27 and 28. No Taiwan or Hong Kong dates have been announced, so overseas fans are still watching for an Asia leg or livestream.

items.en: YOASOBI add two Hong Kong shows to their 11-city Asia-Oceania tour
items.zh: YOASOBI 亞洲巡演加開香港兩場（2027/1/21–22）
items.summary: YOASOBI have confirmed Hong Kong dates for the 11-CITY ASIA-OCEANIA TOUR 2026-2027 'SUPER PLANET', with two nights at AsiaWorld-Arena on January 21 and 22, 2027. The tour takes the duo across Asia and Oceania and is their largest overseas run to date. Local fans have welcomed the second show but are pressing promoters for fairer ticketing after previous sales sold out within minutes and resale prices climbed sharply. For Taiwan-based fans, Hong Kong is the nearest confirmed stop so far, making flight and ticket timing worth planning before the general sale opens.

items.en: Fujii Kaze expands his Prema World Tour to Europe and North America in summer 2027
items.zh: 藤井風 Prema 世界巡演擴及歐美（2027 夏）
items.summary: Fujii Kaze has extended the Prema World Tour with European and North American dates in the summer of 2027, adding to a run that has already taken him through Asian arenas. The tour follows the Prema album and leans on a stripped-back band arrangement that has travelled well with audiences outside Japan. Promoters say demand from overseas listeners has grown steadily through streaming, and the new leg is expected to include major festival slots. Asian dates remain the most accessible option for fans in Taiwan, with ticket details for each market released market by market.
